sentences.text: The name Dermodactylus means "skin finger" because its wings were skin membranes supported by the ring fingers.
The genus is known from a single partial bone found in the hand.
The type specimen, a distal right fourth metacarpal, was found by Samuel Wendell Williston at Como Bluff, Wyoming, in 1878.
When described, this bone was the oldest known, recognized, and described pterosaur remains from North America.
Othniel Charles Marsh originally named the species Pterodactylus montanus.
Dermodactylus was probably about 60 cm long with a wingspan of 1 meter, making it a very small pterosaur.
Dermodactylus was likely a small aerial carnivore.
Dermodactylus had a beak with teeth and likely used them to hunt insects.
Unlike other pterodactyloids, Dermodactylus probably did not live on cliffs or hunt fish.
John Foster estimated the weight of Dermodactylus at 3.3 kg.
The exact placement of Dermodactylus within Pterosauria is uncertain, though it is known to be a pterodactyloid.
Due to the meagerness of the fossil material, Dermodactylus is now regarded as a dubious pterodactyloid.
Dermodactylus lived during the Upper Jurassic (Kimmeridgian-Tithonian) in the Morrison Formation of Wyoming, United States.
